key_insight: GradAudit uses parameter-gradient patterns to identify whether a vision-language model likely learned specific image-text pairs during training, instead of relying on output behavior alone.
clinical_relevance: In healthcare VLLMs, this could help audit whether sensitive patient images and reports were included in training, supporting privacy and provenance checks.
method: Analyze internal parameter gradients on candidate image-text examples
Compare gradient stability and alignment for training-like vs non-training samples
Detect genuine cross-modal associations rather than single-modality membership
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong separation and outperformance over state-of-the-art baselines across medical and general-domain datasets in both pretraining and fine-tuning settings.
watch_item: Gradient-based auditing may be harder to deploy as a routine check because it requires internal model access and can still be affected by model architecture, training stage, or compute cost.
paper_title: Revealing Training Data Exposure in Vision Language Large Models via Parameter Gradients
